reasoning: Recent Montana Senate polling from the last 45 days consistently shows Republican Kurt Alme ahead in the actual four-way general-election field, usually by about 4 to 14 points depending on the poll and matchup. Head-to-head polls are more competitive, but because the official ballot field includes multiple candidates, the current race margin is best characterized as a Republican lead in the low double digits. Montana’s statewide Cook PVI is R+11.

sources.name: Independent Center Voice & Independent Leadership Council statewide survey
sources.details: Statewide Senate survey of likely Montana voters found Alme at 36%, Bodnar at 24%, and Bankhead at 22% in the three-way field.

sources.name: Tavern Research poll (reported by Poll Tracker)
sources.details: Tavern Research poll of Montana Senate voters showed Alme at 49%, Bodnar at 25%, Bankhead at 24%, and Austin at 2% in the full field.

sources.name: Forward Montana Hart Research poll
sources.details: Forward Montana/Hart Research poll reported Alme leading by 16 points in the four-way race at 45% to Bodnar 30%, Bankhead 15%, and Austin 6%.

sources.name: The Atlantic polling summary
sources.details: The Atlantic summarized recent polling as showing Bodnar and Bankhead splitting the non-Alme vote, leaving the Republican with a significant double-digit lead in the four-way field.
